newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trade nil after busy Wed-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trade nil after busy Wed-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. central and southern Plains cattle feedlot markets were quiet early Thursday following active sales Wednesday at $65.00 per cwt which depleted most showlists of market-ready cattle, sources said.
Sales at $65.00 were up $1.00 from light trade on Tuesday and late last week, but steady with tops early last week.
"I imagine trading is over with until Monday," a Texas Panhandle feedlot manager said.
About 67,000 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the weekly figure near 110,000, feedlot sources said.
In Kansas, over 70,000 head sold, which brought the week to date movement near 106,000, the feedlot sources said.
Demand for the cattle reportedly was fueled by active beef movement this week, they said.

Fed cattle prices next week were seen steady to firm in early outlooks, but could change depending on how the market reacts to Friday's USDA monthly cattle on feed report and how strong weekend beef clearance is, several market sources said.
Analysts' estimates for the cattle report peg on-feed supplies as of Aug 1 at an average of 115.6 percent of a year ago from a range of 114.0 to 117.8 percent.
July placement estimates averaged 100.8 percent from a range of 96.0 to 106.5 percent and July marketings at 105.5 percent from 103.0 to 107.0 percent.
